Taping for plantar fasciitis `supports the arch of the foot, limits excessive flattening, and reduces strain on the plantar fascia tissue`.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF18NcB0FV1g92A3zAeNldNt6R2Jvnmb6QRuyuEJ2qPTuTlVwFD_i0VcUg0z3UE2rndkud0MD3314my1qPF3e7UH4ZEYalGZovYLMMmNG-p26yj-6HUsUbUJRd0YP1g851FZkIC92vrmOi2D8EEDGELs1Fi5cXMpSIMtEXToel4rZGRUDYHdtjWEGg_2zxp0GlDEkYQ6IUvDo)

### Choose Your Tape Type

- **Rigid / Zinc Oxide Tape (Low Dye Technique):** Best for strong, inelastic support under full body weight to restrict arch movement during walking or running. Wear for 1 to 5 days, or change daily.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXom-V808HIRTkdX-EmG_VoMlv6JEFC0meYcs-e8qIVXvf6u1M-J4WvxqGLSq4ArMUfqBbb6NRwK1e75_z-qrokeIH2zZ-hC8nrPz8eOsXvGca7hDo6rlVgu9kPfMQhJ-z01B_tiFtuK0j)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF18NcB0FV1g92A3zAeNldNt6R2Jvnmb6QRuyuEJ2qPTuTlVwFD_i0VcUg0z3UE2rndkud0MD3314my1qPF3e7UH4ZEYalGZovYLMMmNG-p26yj-6HUsUbUJRd0YP1g851FZkIC92vrmOi2D8EEDGELs1Fi5cXMpSIMtEXToel4rZGRUDYHdtjWEGg_2zxp0GlDEkYQ6IUvDo)
- **Kinesiology Tape (K-Tape):** Provides elastic support, mild compression, and dynamic feedback while allowing a fuller range of motion. Usually worn for 3 to 4 days.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX-xUHpQgV2bglK8EZd9nxdfq7vRAKLrk7YxQKVcgr8eT9S9mEqe_BJkyGQLzRGq2FVT4SluseBylwKuEX2rg99M43K5Ati2CfnNOWt-8vtYcKcWGL8zPtGeTKL5vo1hyxKOj25BqXEwxJ5aN_KCPwxjo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXZQiR1ovo4L58yqBnFB_9KCeQIHthxa1AQvSKZuop6KhYqbbyKjd0PG_9VrXjtjO-rdyKArbICgWB-DG_6Eo5oFlLcnG67SlA9zi2ntqomQdXGXbMi0Ep1KhdQ36Hb7e4_mIN)

### How to Apply Kinesiology Tape (Basic Method)

1. **Prepare the skin:** Wash your foot with a non-moisturizing soap, dry it completely, and trim excess hair if needed.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqwEBxCJF107L4MeJxodxihAchi9040c1Z311dqEBM6T5Etz5JTVCoJLaR8CbVkp6y4wAdgroMiG_FOViYpPOjtUqMcVIgfcsMF8WEgW79Gb3kJG37C4vCBzqx0BoVL2unMcenrkyF9IFkU_HlnDmiuM7iHQW-SlCOWvnYykxeevyAK73JLEA-XpeL7QY_Xdc7g4HDc2I42OE1sCoCSHdxgKZXLmBTx__jv21fHY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX-xUHpQgV2bglK8EZd9nxdfq7vRAKLrk7YxQKVcgr8eT9S9mEqe_BJkyGQLzRGq2FVT4SluseBylwKuEX2rg99M43K5Ati2CfnNOWt-8vtYcKcWGL8zPtGeTKL5vo1hyxKOj25BqXEwxJ5aN_KCPwxjo)
2. **Position the foot:** Flex your foot toward your shin (dorsiflexion) to stretch the plantar fascia along the bottom of the foot.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXCVTkkzYuwLeJR55nKqVh5Q2SSfUpxg8H_Sa4Sj9bRWMecROTFLcAZ1Derqj2Rc_Rzm7EKppla96QwatvTdf2VpJ8ICcHALgiSwhgUGtzjCNFFcrxjC3GJ9J-ZjmbTMII-fo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX-xUHpQgV2bglK8EZd9nxdfq7vRAKLrk7YxQKVcgr8eT9S9mEqe_BJkyGQLzRGq2FVT4SluseBylwKuEX2rg99M43K5Ati2CfnNOWt-8vtYcKcWGL8zPtGeTKL5vo1hyxKOj25BqXEwxJ5aN_KCPwxjo)
3. **Apply the main strip (Full Strip ~8 inches):** 
	- Peel a 2-inch backing paper to create an anchor and stick it with **0% stretch** on the ball of the foot.
	- Apply the middle section with **50% moderate stretch** along the sole and around the heel.
	- Lay the final end near the lower leg or heel with **0% stretch**.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXlnLb3NXSpeUNyPwb0iyIFYGywDDf_O-9isFytHClySdYQb6zVBoKuqtnnDQs5P6C7lDSzrsuqEJhq0i5wvsoToFAddh2xobchreasVzi_zqZrzWLIFm3yiIOXrjTTAL7FUEM0LHhpQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX-xUHpQgV2bglK8EZd9nxdfq7vRAKLrk7YxQKVcgr8eT9S9mEqe_BJkyGQLzRGq2FVT4SluseBylwKuEX2rg99M43K5Ati2CfnNOWt-8vtYcKcWGL8zPtGeTKL5vo1hyxKOj25BqXEwxJ5aN_KCPwxjo)
4. **Apply support strips (Half Strips ~5 inches):** 
	- Tear the backing paper in the center, stretch the middle section moderately, and place it across the bottom of the foot directly in front of or behind your primary pain point.
	- Rub the entire tape application to activate the heat-sensitive adhesive and wait about an hour before heavy activity.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXLgauPOKpJ1NW4MlAj6pf0SeByG5ZOiof31duQGnydrJdQ-N_PxMG_M3aqtpbPF_71qvbs8dFQ5zLsFoU2XFYIdnWE7-L79-ipkE3CLgLVq_e5R0bm3kbnKJ6X31_ZaKasgLYMFrdp_8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXCVTkkzYuwLeJR55nKqVh5Q2SSfUpxg8H_Sa4Sj9bRWMecROTFLcAZ1Derqj2Rc_Rzm7EKppla96QwatvTdf2VpJ8ICcHALgiSwhgUGtzjCNFFcrxjC3GJ9J-ZjmbTMII-fo)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX-xUHpQgV2bglK8EZd9nxdfq7vRAKLrk7YxQKVcgr8eT9S9mEqe_BJkyGQLzRGq2FVT4SluseBylwKuEX2rg99M43K5Ati2CfnNOWt-8vtYcKcWGL8zPtGeTKL5vo1hyxKOj25BqXEwxJ5aN_KCPwxjo)

### Important Safety Tips

- Remove the tape immediately if you notice itching, redness, or skin irritation.
- If you have diabetes or poor circulation, consult a doctor or podiatrist before using adhesive taping to avoid skin damage.
- For structured guidelines on low-rigid methods, see the [Royal Orthopaedic Hospital Low Dye Guide](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF18NcB0FV1g92A3zAeNldNt6R2Jvnmb6QRuyuEJ2qPTuTlVwFD_i0VcUg0z3UE2rndkud0MD3314my1qPF3e7UH4ZEYalGZovYLMMmNG-p26yj-6HUsUbUJRd0YP1g851FZkIC92vrmOi2D8EEDGELs1Fi5cXMpSIMtEXToel4rZGRUDYHdtjWEGg_2zxp0GlDEkYQ6IUvDo).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXCVTkkzYuwLeJR55nKqVh5Q2SSfUpxg8H_Sa4Sj9bRWMecROTFLcAZ1Derqj2Rc_Rzm7EKppla96QwatvTdf2VpJ8ICcHALgiSwhgUGtzjCNFFcrxjC3GJ9J-ZjmbTMII-fo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXWoQyY8FtjLil_nY6IetYuOEBUjjuRwsFTJpGGhnSVCtix8k3pr6WsX6K5gKAIaWO2rlVHyj0w-oZy2yrGPjRWtUhlurw1uKsqyr9EyGZUgCkb9WruAljqGfEUinp8ePZ7H4m)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF18NcB0FV1g92A3zAeNldNt6R2Jvnmb6QRuyuEJ2qPTuTlVwFD_i0VcUg0z3UE2rndkud0MD3314my1qPF3e7UH4ZEYalGZovYLMMmNG-p26yj-6HUsUbUJRd0YP1g851FZkIC92vrmOi2D8EEDGELs1Fi5cXMpSIMtEXToel4rZGRUDYHdtjWEGg_2zxp0GlDEkYQ6IUvDo)
